vocabulary.meaning_en: the study of things that happened in the past
vocabulary.example: I love reading about the history of my country.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make something feel real and interesting
vocabulary.example: This museum brings history to life.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a lot to do
vocabulary.example: She is too busy with work to visit.

vocabulary.meaning_en: outside, not in a building
vocabulary.example: We like working outdoors in spring.

vocabulary.meaning_en: needing rest or sleep
vocabulary.example: I'm tired after a long day at work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a picture, film or text that tells people about a product or event
vocabulary.example: I saw an advertisement for a new phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where people watch plays and shows
vocabulary.note_ar: theater أمريكي، theatre بريطاني (وفي اسم Ford's Theatre).
vocabulary.example: We saw a show at the theater.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where people can see important old or special things
vocabulary.example: The museum is open every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a play or performance people watch
vocabulary.example: The new show starts at eight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stop living
vocabulary.example: Abraham Lincoln died in 1865.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make you remember something
vocabulary.example: This photo reminds me of my school days.

vocabulary.meaning_en: quiet and thoughtful; not joking
vocabulary.example: He was a serious child.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an outdoor place where children play
vocabulary.example: The kids are at the playground.

vocabulary.meaning_en: funny in a childish way; not serious
vocabulary.example: Stop making silly faces!

vocabulary.meaning_en: seats that hang from ropes or chains for children to move back and forth
vocabulary.example: My little sister loves the swings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a smooth slope children go down at a playground
vocabulary.example: The children went down the slide.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long board that goes up and down with a child on each end
vocabulary.example: Two kids played on the teeter-totter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the leader of a country (or a company)
vocabulary.example: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the time when you are a child
vocabulary.example: I had a happy childhood.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a hope or plan for the future
vocabulary.note_en: A dream come true = something you hoped for that really happens.
vocabulary.example: Her dream is to be a doctor.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who travels into space
vocabulary.example: The astronaut flew to the space station.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large round object that moves around a star
vocabulary.example: Earth is a planet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the area outside the Earth's air
vocabulary.example: He wants to fly into outer space.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having great value
vocabulary.example: Sleep is important for your health.

vocabulary.meaning_en: truly; used to show you are telling the truth
vocabulary.example: Honestly, I didn't know.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to hurt or kill with a gun
vocabulary.example: A man shot President Lincoln at Ford's Theatre.

fine_lines.title: outdoors vs outdoor
fine_lines.explanation_ar: outdoors ظرف يأتي بعد الفعل: work outdoors (يعمل في الخارج). outdoor صفة تأتي قبل الاسم: an outdoor market.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Outdoors is an adverb; it comes after a verb: work outdoors. Outdoor is an adjective; it comes before a noun: an outdoor market.

examples.sentence: We ate at an outdoor café.

fine_lines.title: silly vs serious
fine_lines.explanation_ar: متضادتان. silly = غير جاد / طفولي ومضحك. serious = جاد ويفكر كثيراً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: They are opposites. Silly = not serious, childish and funny. Serious = thoughtful, not joking.

examples.sentence: Anna was a tall, serious child.

fine_lines.title: history vs story
fine_lines.explanation_ar: history = أحداث حقيقية من الماضي أو مادة دراسة التاريخ. story = قصة (حقيقية أو خيالية).
fine_lines.explanation_en: History = real events of the past, or the school subject. Story = a tale, true or not.

examples.sentence: I studied the history of Washington, D.C.
My grandmother told me a story.

expressions.example: Come in and have a seat.
"I have to work late." "That's too bad."
Hi, Sam! How are you these days?
We have a lot to do. Let's get to work.
That smell reminds me of my mother's kitchen.

expressions.phrase: When I was a little girl…
expressions.meaning_en: A way to start talking about your childhood.
expressions.example: When I was a little boy, I loved trains.

expressions.meaning_en: Please don't make fun of what I say.
expressions.example: Don't laugh! I really wanted to be a pilot.
"I read every book in the library." "I can believe that."

expressions.phrase: Guess what I wanted to be?
expressions.meaning_ar: خمّن ماذا كنت أريد أن أصبح؟
expressions.meaning_en: Try to guess my childhood dream.
expressions.example: Guess what I wanted to be? A teacher!

expressions.meaning_en: do what we always hoped to do
expressions.example: Hard work can help you make your dreams come true.

grammar.title: Simple past: was / were
grammar.explanation_ar: ماضي الفعل be: was مع I / he / she / it، و were مع you / we / they. النفي: wasn't / weren't. نستخدمه لوصف الأشخاص والأشياء في الماضي: I was a tall, serious child.
grammar.explanation_en: The past of be: was with I / he / she / it, and were with you / we / they. Negative: wasn't / weren't. Use it to describe people and things in the past.
examples: I was a tall, serious child.
I was not like other children.
Today was a busy day at work.

grammar.title: Simple past: regular verbs with -ed
grammar.explanation_ar: معظم الأفعال تأخذ ed في الماضي: play → played، love → loved، want → wanted. إذا انتهى الفعل بحرف ساكن + y نحوّلها إلى ied: study → studied. والفعل نفسه مع كل الضمائر. انتبه للنطق: played /d/، wanted /ɪd/، laughed /t/.
grammar.explanation_en: Most verbs add -ed in the past: play → played, love → loved, want → wanted. Consonant + y becomes -ied: study → studied. Same form for all subjects. Pronunciation: played /d/, wanted /ɪd/, laughed /t/.
examples: The other children played silly games.
I loved to read serious books.
I studied the stars and planets.

grammar.title: When + past: talking about childhood
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم When I was a kid / a little girl لنتحدث عن الطفولة، ثم فعل في الماضي. ومع wanted to be + مهنة نتحدث عن أحلامنا القديمة.
grammar.explanation_en: Use "When I was a kid / a little girl" + a past verb to talk about childhood. Use "wanted to be" + a job to talk about old dreams.
examples: When I was a kid, I studied the stars.
I wanted to be President of the United States.
When I was young, I wanted to be an astronaut.

questions.question: When I ___ a little girl, I loved books.
questions.explanation_ar: مع I في الماضي نستخدم was.
questions.explanation_en: With "I" in the past we use "was".

questions.question: The other children ___ silly games.
questions.explanation_ar: نضيف ed إلى play فتصبح played.

questions.question: When I was a kid, I ___ to be an astronaut.
questions.explanation_ar: نتحدث عن الطفولة في الماضي، فنستخدم wanted to be.
questions.explanation_en: We talk about childhood in the past, so we use "wanted to be".

questions.question: An astronaut travels into ___.
questions.explanation_ar: رائد الفضاء يسافر إلى الفضاء الخارجي.
questions.explanation_en: An astronaut travels into outer space.

questions.question: A building where you can see important old things is a ___.
questions.explanation_ar: المتحف museum مبنى نرى فيه أشياء قديمة ومهمة.
questions.explanation_en: A museum is a building where people see important old things.

questions.question: We ate lunch at an ___ market.
questions.explanation_en: Before a noun we use the adjective "outdoor".

questions.question: "That advertisement reminds me of something" means:
Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation_en: We use "were" with we, you and they.
